clinical_status: widely used research biomarker; no FDA-cleared quantitative assay
notes: Also called 8-OHdG. The anchor analyte. Urinary level reflects whole-body repair flux; DNA-hydrolysate level reflects steady-state lesion burden - the two are NOT interchangeable

clinical_status: research biomarker with prospective outcome data
notes: Independently associated with long-term mortality in type 2 diabetes; rises with metabolic/mitochondrial stress even when 8-oxodG is normal
Free base is released by glycosylase action and by nucleotide-pool sanitisation (NUDT1/MTH1); rising 8-oxoGua with rising 8-oxodG indicates competent excision rather than repair failure
Formed preferentially at low oxygen tension where 8-oxoG formation is disfavoured; including it prevents systematic under-reporting of purine oxidation in hypoxic tissue
CRITICAL INTERPRETIVE TRAP: 5-hmdC is both an oxidation product and a programmed TET-generated epigenetic mark. Must be interpreted against 5-medC; never scored as damage alone
Not a damage marker. Included so that 5-hmdC can be expressed as a fraction of its precursor pool and TET activity separated from oxidative chemistry
Substrate of NTHL1/NEIL1 rather than OGG1 - gives an independent read on the non-OGG1 arm of base excision repair

clinical_status: research use; mechanistically tied to a clinical test
role_in_panel: direct link to MGMT repair module
notes: The specific substrate of MGMT. Pairing this analyte with MGMT promoter methylation is the tightest damage-to-repair coupling in the whole panel
Most abundant alkylation adduct; depurinates spontaneously so it is recovered in urine. Reports alkylating exposure burden (tobacco; nitrosamines; chemotherapy)
Formed from malondialdehyde; converts a lipid-peroxidation signal into a covalent DNA lesion. Links the isoprostane read-out to genuine genotoxicity
Derived from lipid peroxidation aldehydes and vinyl-monomer exposure; the only adenine-directed lesion in the panel
Denominator for all DNA-hydrolysate lesions; results reported as lesions per 10^6 dG. Also the substrate-pool check that hydrolysis went to completion
Denominator for all spot-urine analytes. Mandatory - unnormalised spot-urine adduct concentrations are not comparable between subjects

clinical_status: research biomarker with pooled reference values
notes: Not a DNA lesion. Included to separate systemic oxidative stress from DNA-specific damage. Pooled IQR 0.18-0.40 ug/g creatinine by chemical methods in adults with BMI below 25

species_type: cyclic nucleoside (C5'-C8 bond; sugar not cleavable)
role_in_panel: oxidative lesion that reports NER rather than BER
notes: Formed by hydroxyl radical attack followed by intramolecular C5'-C8 cyclisation. The covalent sugar-base bond distorts the duplex and makes the lesion a NER substrate rather than a BER substrate. Same oxidant source as 8-oxodG but a different repair pathway - this is the analyte that lets one oxidant stress interrogate two pathways. Blocks polymerases and inhibits gene expression; accumulates with disease

species_type: cyclic nucleoside (C5'-C8 bond; sugar not cleavable)
role_in_panel: NER-reporting oxidative lesion; guanine counterpart of cdA
notes: Guanine analogue of cdA from the same chemistry. Measured as R and S diastereomers, which must be resolved chromatographically and summed or reported separately

Product of hypochlorous acid from myeloperoxidase in activated neutrophils. Chemically distinct from oxidation and from nitration, so it separates neutrophil-driven inflammatory DNA damage from general oxidative stress. Chlorine isotope pattern (35Cl/37Cl 3:1) gives a built-in confirmation ion

Arises from cytosine deamination and from dUTP misincorporation under folate deficiency or thymidylate-synthase inhibition. Neither oxidative nor alkylative - adds a third damage mechanism. Its repair enzymes UNG and SMUG1 are already in the expression panel
